headline: Going Commando reaches 7,100 matched USA v1.01 functions
summary: Contributors can build more of Going Commando from C after an 842-function import from bigbeno37's fork (#368). The final progress report puts USA v1.01 at 7,100 of 8,578 functions and 3,637,728 of 5,525,780 code bytes, or 65.83% by code size. The day's progress commit also records USA v2.00 at 6,646 of 8,634 functions and PAL at 4,979 of 8,672. Matching means the compiled function has exactly the original game's bytes.
highlights: #368 contributes 609,116 USA v1.01 code bytes and dominates the day's line totals with 73,572 additions and 59,161 deletions. Its author credits Claude-assisted work in the fork.

Reviewed integration retains 15 contributor functions, including work in Todano, Aranos prison and Endako, while keeping an unsafe hit-vector reconstruction out of matching code (#361, #363, #365, #366).
Before the large import, #367 reported matched code at 54.81% for USA v1.01, 32.09% for USA v2.00 and 17.49% for PAL. Those are intermediate figures.
Parallel builds give each simultaneous program its own Wine prefix, removing a shared assembler/linker bottleneck. #369 fixes fully linked code accounting to sum completed units.
Object-slot lookup and held-object routines were proposed in #370 and #371, with no landing recorded today.
